unit.label: Plans & invitations
unit.title: Let’s Make a Plan Together
unit.description: 8 new words and expressions. Give opinions, invite someone, and agree on a day and activity.

goal.text: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？
goal.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù yóuyǒng, zěnmeyàng?
goal.meaning: How about going swimming together tomorrow?

unit.bookReference: Book 1 · Lesson 3: days, opinions, invitations & possibilities

lessons.title: Today or Tomorrow?
lessons.subtitle: Give a familiar activity a day

steps.prompt: In 我週末常游泳, what does 常 add?
steps.explanation: 常 describes how frequently the activity happens.

steps.prompt: A friend writes 我明天去游泳. Which day is the plan?
steps.explanation: 明天 places the activity tomorrow.

lessons.title: What Do You Think?
lessons.subtitle: Say whether an activity is fun

steps.explanation: 照相 is the activity; 照片 is the photo.

steps.prompt: Which component is on the right of 玩?
steps.explanation: 玩 has the jade component 王 on the left and 元 on the right.

steps.prompt: What does 我覺得游泳很好玩 tell us?
steps.explanation: 覺得 introduces what the speaker thinks. It does not confirm a plan.

lessons.title: Do It Together
lessons.subtitle: Invite someone to share the activity

steps.prompt: What does 一起 add in 我們一起看電影?
steps.explanation: 一起 makes this a shared activity. 都 only tells us everyone is included.

steps.prompt: A: 你要不要喝茶？ B: 不要。 What does B say?
steps.explanation: 不要 answers a question with 要不要.

lessons.title: How Does That Sound?
lessons.subtitle: Ask for a reaction and accept a plan

steps.prompt: Your friend proposes a plan and adds 怎麼樣. What response clearly accepts?
steps.explanation: 好啊 is a warm acceptance. 不想去 declines the plan.

lessons.title: What Can This Help You Do?
lessons.subtitle: Explain one possible benefit

steps.explanation: 會 can describe a skill someone has learned.

steps.prompt: What does 看電影可以學中文 mean here?
options: Movies can be a way to learn Chinese
steps.answer: Movies can be a way to learn Chinese
steps.explanation: 可以 introduces a possibility or benefit; it does not claim mastery.

lessons.title: Agree on a Plan
lessons.subtitle: Follow a short invitation and counteroffer

steps.prompt: What does 我不想去游泳 express?
steps.explanation: 不想 + activity expresses a decision or desire.

steps.prompt: A: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？ B: 我不想去游泳。我們一起看電影吧。 What is B suggesting?
steps.explanation: B declines swimming, then suggests watching a movie together.

steps.prompt: A: 好啊！我們今天一起看電影。 Which day is now agreed?
steps.explanation: The final acceptance explicitly says 今天. It changes the earlier proposal’s day.

steps.prompt: Which reply clearly accepts the invitation?
steps.explanation: An opinion or habit can support a conversation, but 好啊 clearly accepts.

lessons.title: Unit 8 Review
lessons.subtitle: Time, opinion, invitation, and an agreed plan

steps.prompt: A: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？ B: 好啊！ What have they agreed?
steps.explanation: B accepts the complete plan: time, company, and activity.

newVocabulary.meaning: how about it?; how does that sound?

今.note: 今 begins 今天, today. Learn the time word as a whole.
今.memory: 今 has a spreading roof, a dot beneath it, and a bent final stroke. Keep that dot separate from the lower bend; do not add the extra dot of 令.

parts.label: top
parts.name: spreading roof
parts.description: The first two sloping strokes meet at the top and open outward, making space beneath their meeting point.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: dot and bend
parts.description: Place a small dot under the roof, then the single bent final stroke below it. These are two separate strokes.

天.meaning: day; sky (in 今天 and 明天)
天.note: 明天 (míngtiān) means tomorrow. 天 has two horizontal strokes above two spreading slants. Compare it with 大: 天 has an extra horizontal across the top.
天.memory: 天 has two horizontal strokes above two spreading slants. Compare it with 大: 天 has an extra horizontal across the top.

parts.label: 天
parts.name: 天 component
parts.description: Write the short top horizontal, the longer horizontal below, then the two sloping strokes that spread into a broad base.

明.note: 明 begins 明天, tomorrow. Its shapes are 日 and 月.
明.memory: 明 places 日 on the left and the taller 月 on the right. Compare the closed bottom of 日 with the longer downward strokes of 月.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: sun-shaped left side
parts.description: Make the four strokes of 日 on the left, including its short inner horizontal. Keep it narrower than the whole character.

parts.label: 月
parts.name: moon-shaped right side
parts.description: 月 uses four strokes on the right. Its long outer strokes surround two short horizontal strokes.

覺.note: 覺得 (juéde) means think; feel (an opinion). 覺 has the same complex upper group you saw in 學, but 見 underneath instead of 子. The lower 見 contains 目 above two spreading legs.
覺.memory: 覺 has the same complex upper group you saw in 學, but 見 underneath instead of 子. The lower 見 contains 目 above two spreading legs.

parts.label: upper
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper thirteen strokes form the covered group shared with 學. Keep its small inner crossing strokes compact.

parts.label: 見
parts.name: 見 component
parts.description: The lower seven strokes form 見: a tall eye-shaped 目 with two legs below. This lower group distinguishes 覺 from 學.

得.meaning: light final syllable in 覺得
得.note: 覺得 (juéde) means think; feel (an opinion). 得 has 彳 on the left and a stacked right side: 日, a horizontal, and 寸. In 覺得, say the final de lightly; other words can use dé or děi.
得.memory: 得 has 彳 on the left and a stacked right side: 日, a horizontal, and 寸. In 覺得, say the final de lightly; other words can use dé or děi.

parts.label: 彳
parts.name: 彳 component
parts.description: The left component has two short slants and a vertical. Keep its three strokes narrow alongside the taller right-hand stack.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group
parts.description: The eight strokes on the right stack 日 over a horizontal and 寸. Notice the small dot beside the lower hooked vertical.

玩.note: 玩 has a second tone in 好玩, fun. 好玩 describes an activity as enjoyable.
玩.memory: 玩 puts the narrow jade component 王 beside 元. On the right, notice two horizontal bars above two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: jade component
parts.description: The left side looks like a narrow 王. As a component here it represents jade; its final stroke rises toward the right.

parts.label: 元
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 元 has two horizontal strokes above two legs, the right one ending in a hook. Leave space between those lower strokes.

起.note: 起 completes 一起, together. 一起 goes before the shared action.
起.memory: 起 combines 走 with 巳 tucked at the right. The long final stroke of 走 sweeps beneath the right-hand component.

parts.label: 走
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: The seven strokes of 走 occupy the left and lower part. Its sweeping base extends under the whole character.

parts.label: 巳
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: The three strokes of 巳 fit on the right above the sweeping base. In this Taiwan form, notice the closed upper space.

起.partOrderLabel: 走 first, then 巳 on the right

怎.note: 怎 first appears in 怎麼樣 (zěnmeyàng), how does that sound? Learn the whole expression together.
怎.memory: Remember 怎 as 乍 above 心: a compact top with a wider heart shape below.

parts.label: 乍
parts.name: upper part
parts.description: 乍 has a short slant at the top and horizontal strokes extending right from a vertical.

parts.label: 心
parts.name: heart component
parts.description: 心 sits below 乍, with dots around a curved hook.

樣.note: 怎麼樣 (zěnmeyàng) means how does that sound?. 樣 puts 木 beside 羕. The right side has a sheep-shaped upper group over a branching, water-like lower group with a central hook.
樣.memory: 樣 puts 木 beside 羕. The right side has a sheep-shaped upper group over a branching, water-like lower group with a central hook.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: 木 component
parts.description: 木 is the four-stroke tree component on the left. Its final stroke becomes compact beside the wider right component.

parts.label: 羕
parts.name: 羕 component
parts.description: The eleven right-hand strokes form 羕. Keep the upper horizontal bars orderly and leave room for the branching lower strokes.

啊.note: 好啊 (hǎo a) means sure!; OK!. 啊 has a small mouth 口 on the left and 阿 on the right. Inside 阿, notice the narrow ear-shaped component beside 可.
啊.memory: 啊 has a small mouth 口 on the left and 阿 on the right. Inside 阿, notice the narrow ear-shaped component beside 可.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: 口 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make a small mouth component, a useful clue for a particle used in speech.

parts.label: 阿
parts.name: 阿 component
parts.description: The right eight strokes form 阿: a narrow left-side 阝 followed by 可. Keep the small inner box of 可 distinct.

可.note: 可 begins 可以. Here 可以 describes a possibility, not a learned skill.
可.memory: 可 has a long top bar, a small 口 beneath it, and a final vertical hook on the right. Keep the small box inside the space under the bar.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: bar, box, and right hook
parts.description: Write the top horizontal, then the three strokes of the small 口, and finish with the long right-side vertical hook.

以.note: 可以 (kěyǐ) means can (possibility). 以 has a short vertical and a rising stroke on the left, a separate dot in the middle, and two longer sloping strokes on the right. In this Taiwan form, the left side takes two strokes.
以.memory: 以 has a short vertical and a rising stroke on the left, a separate dot in the middle, and two longer sloping strokes on the right. In this Taiwan form, the left side takes two strokes.

parts.label: 以
parts.name: 以 component
parts.description: Write the short left vertical, then the rising stroke, then the central dot. Finish with the two longer right-hand strokes. This source Taiwan form has five strokes, not four.

u8-time.title: Today or tomorrow
u8-time.pattern: subject + 今天 / 明天 + activity
u8-time.explanation: 今天 (jīntiān) means today; 明天 (míngtiān) means tomorrow. Both share 天. Reuse the time position you learned with 週末: put 今天 or 明天 before the activity. Time can go just after the subject or at the beginning. No extra word is needed for English “on” or “will.” The building prompt tells you which subject/time order to use.

examples.meaning: We are going to see a movie today.

u8-time.remember: 今天 is today. 明天 is tomorrow. Both time expressions go before the action.

u8-opinion.title: Say what you think about an activity
u8-opinion.pattern: person + 覺得 + activity + 很好玩
u8-opinion.explanation: 覺得 (juéde) introduces an opinion: “I think / I feel that…” 好玩 (hǎowán) means fun or enjoyable. 我覺得游泳很好玩 contains a complete idea after 覺得: 游泳很好玩, swimming is fun. The activity is what you describe. Reuse 很 before the description, without 是. 想 + action already means “want to”; 覺得 + statement tells us your opinion instead. No extra word for English “that” is needed.

examples.meaning: She thinks taking photos is fun.

u8-opinion.remember: 想游泳: want to swim. 覺得游泳很好玩: think swimming is fun.

u8-not-fun.title: Disagree with an opinion
u8-not-fun.explanation: 好玩 is a description, like 好看. Put 不 directly before 好玩 to say “not fun.” In this basic negative description, do not keep 很. Compare 不好玩, not fun, with 不想去, do not want to go: an opinion about the activity and a decision about going are different messages.

examples.meaning: I think taking photos is not fun.
I do not want to go take photos.

u8-not-fun.remember: Disagree with the description using 不好玩. Decline an activity using the familiar 不想 + action.

u8-together.title: Make it a shared activity
u8-together.pattern: subject + time + 一起 + 去 + activity
u8-together.explanation: 一起 (yìqǐ) means together: the people do the activity with one another. Put it before 去 or another action, not at the end as in English. 我們都去 says everyone goes; 我們一起去 says we go together. Everyone could go separately, so 都 and 一起 are not interchangeable. 一 is pronounced yì before the third tone qǐ.

examples.meaning: We are going swimming together tomorrow.

u8-together.remember: Time comes before 一起; 一起 comes before the action.

u8-invite.title: Ask how the plan sounds
u8-invite.explanation: 怎麼樣 (zěnmeyàng) asks “How does that sound?” after a proposed plan. First say what you suggest, then ask for the other person’s reaction. 好啊 (hǎo a), “Sure!” or “OK!”, accepts warmly. 啊 is a light sentence-final particle; here learn it as part of 好啊. You already know 吧 for a suggestion; 怎麼樣 explicitly asks the listener to respond. Do not add 嗎 after this question.

examples.text: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù yóuyǒng, zěnmeyàng?
examples.meaning: How about going swimming together tomorrow?

u8-invite.remember: Offer a concrete plan, ask 怎麼樣, then listen for acceptance or another suggestion.

u8-possible.title: Say what an activity lets you do
u8-possible.explanation: 可以 (kěyǐ) here means can in the sense of possibility. 看電影可以學中文 says watching movies can be a way to learn Chinese. The first activity is what the sentence is about; 可以 introduces what becomes possible through it. This does not say watching one movie guarantees fluency. You already know 會 for an acquired skill, as in 我會說中文. 可以 in this lesson explains an opportunity or possible benefit, not that someone has mastered a skill.

examples.meaning: Watching movies can be a way to learn Chinese.
Listening to Chinese can be a way to learn Chinese.

u8-possible.remember: First name the activity; then 可以 + what it enables. Keep 會 for the learned-skill meaning you already know.

u8-counteroffer.title: Turn a declined plan into an alternative
u8-counteroffer.pattern: 不想 + first activity；suggest another plan
u8-counteroffer.explanation: Use the language you know to negotiate a plan in small steps. 不想 declines the proposed activity. A second sentence with 一起 and 吧 offers another plan. The listener can accept with 好啊. There is no new word for “instead” here: the order of the two sentences makes the alternative clear. An opinion with 覺得 can explain why someone likes a proposal, but does not by itself confirm they will attend.

examples.text: 我不想去游泳。我們一起看電影吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng qù yóuyǒng. Wǒmen yìqǐ kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.meaning: I do not want to go swimming. Let’s watch a movie together.

examples.text: 好啊！我們今天一起看電影。
examples.pinyin: Hǎo a! Wǒmen jīntiān yìqǐ kàn diànyǐng.
examples.meaning: Sure! We will watch a movie together today.

u8-counteroffer.remember: Track what is only proposed and what both people finally agree to do.

u8-fun.note: 覺得 introduces the statement 游泳很好玩.

u8-photo-fun.meaning: She thinks taking photos is fun.
u8-photo-fun.note: 照相 is the activity being described.

u8-not-fun.meaning: I think taking photos is not fun.
u8-not-fun.note: The negative description is 不好玩, without 很.

u8-together.meaning: We are going swimming together tomorrow. Start with “we.”
u8-together.note: Time, then 一起, then 去 and its activity.

u8-invite.text: 我們明天一起去游泳，怎麼樣？
u8-invite.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù yóuyǒng, zěnmeyàng?
u8-invite.meaning: How about going swimming together tomorrow? Start with “we.”
u8-invite.note: The plan comes first; 怎麼樣 asks for a reaction at the end.

u8-accept.note: 好啊 warmly accepts the proposal.

u8-learn.meaning: Watching movies can be a way to learn Chinese.
u8-learn.note: 看電影 is the activity; 可以學中文 gives its possible benefit.

u8-listen-learn.meaning: Listening to Chinese can be a way to learn Chinese.
u8-listen-learn.note: 中文 appears twice: what you listen to, then what you can learn.

u8-counteroffer.note: In the conversation, this is the alternative to swimming.

u8-tomorrow.meaning: I am going swimming tomorrow. Start with “I.”
u8-tomorrow.note: The subject comes first, then 明天, then the activity.

u8-today.meaning: We are going to see a movie today. Start with “today.”
u8-today.note: This version puts 今天 before the subject. Both stand before the action.

u8-want-together.pinyin: Nǐ yào bu yào yìqǐ kàn diànyǐng?
u8-want-together.meaning: Would you like to watch a movie together?
u8-want-together.note: Reuse 要不要 with the shared activity. Do not add 嗎.

u8-final-plan.meaning: We will watch a movie together today. Start with “we.”
u8-final-plan.note: The agreed plan includes the people, time, and shared activity.
